text: Tonight. Macau.
Over ten thousand lights. All for one ball.
That ball first touched a court in China forty-seven years ago.
Summer, 1979.
Diplomatic ties: six months old.
A team of NBA champions stepped off a plane.
They had seen the biggest arenas. The toughest opponents.
But in Beijing, they looked up.
Seven-foot-six. Mu Tiezhu.
Ten years later, an American waited nearly an hour in a guard booth at China's state television.
His name: David Stern.
All he had was a videotape.
And a generation discovered basketball on tape.
In 2002, that generation produced a giant.
say: In two thousand two, that generation produced a giant!

text: October 14, 2004. Shanghai.
say: October fourteenth, two thousand four. Shanghai.

text: The first NBA game ever played in China.
say: The first NBA game ever played in China!

text: A Rockets executive called it the Beatles meets Michael Jordan.
say: A Rockets executive called it, the Beatles meets Michael Jordan!

text: The next fifteen years.
Seventeen teams. Twenty-eight games.
LeBron came.
Kobe came.
Even Michael Jordan came.
Then, the lights went out.
2,190 days. Not a single China Game.
say: Two thousand one hundred ninety days. Not a single China Game.

text: But the ball never stopped bouncing.
2025. Macau.
It's back.
This year, the Rockets return.
The team that started it all.
say: The team that started it all!

text: Forty-seven years. And the ball keeps bouncing.
